title: Linear upper bound conjecture for the longest solvable board
statement:
For an odd integer $n\geq 3$, let $ML(n)$ be the maximum length of a solvable board of size $n$:

$$
ML(n):=\max_{A\in Sol_n}\{\operatorname{length} A\}.
$$

**Linear upper bound conjecture.** As $n\to\infty$, $ML(n)=O(n)$.

The construction preceding this conjecture gives solvable boards of length $3n$ for all odd $n\geq 11$, while the trivial general upper bound is $ML(n)\leq n^2$. The conjecture asserts that the maximal length grows only linearly with the board size.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.05416

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2021).
source_name: Ary Shaviv, “Board games, random boards and long boards”, arXiv:2110.05416 (2021).
